ai_explanation.concept_rule: The midpoint of two points in 3D space with coordinates $(x_1, y_1, z_1)$ and $(x_2, y_2, z_2)$ is given by $\left(\frac{x_1+x_2}{2}, \frac{y_1+y_2}{2}, \frac{z_1+z_2}{2}\right)$.
step_by_step: Take the coordinates of points A$(0, 4, 6)$ and D$(-10, 4, 6)$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Sign errors when averaging negative coordinates.

mark_breakdown.desc: Calculate distances DM and CD using the 3D distance formula
Set up tan ratio for angle CMD
Calculate angle CMD to obtain approximately 55.3°

subparts.solution:
Let $\text{C}\hat{\text{M}}\text{D}$ be $\theta$.
Now $\text{DM} = 5\text{ units}$
and
$$\text{CD} = \sqrt{(-10 - (-10))^2 + (4 - 0)^2 + (6 - 0)^2} = \sqrt{0^2 + 4^2 + 6^2} = \sqrt{52}\text{ units}$$
$$\therefore \tan\theta = \frac{\sqrt{52}}{5}$$
$$\therefore \theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{52}}{5}\right) \approx 55.3^{\circ}$$
$$\therefore \text{C}\hat{\text{M}}\text{D} \approx 55.3^{\circ}$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: In a right-angled triangle in 3D space, calculate the lengths of the two legs using coordinate differences, then use the tangent ratio.
step_by_step: Recognize $\Delta \text{CDM}$ is right-angled at D, so $\tan\theta = \frac{\text{CD}}{\text{DM}} = \frac{\sqrt{52}}{5}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Identifying the wrong vertex as the right angle.

subparts.stem: Find the angle between the following line segments and the base plane BECO: [OD]

mark_breakdown.desc: Identify coordinates of point N and compute distances DN and NO
Set up tan ratio for angle DON

subparts.solution:
The required angle is $\text{D}\hat{\text{O}}\text{N}$, where $\text{N}$ has coordinates $(-10, 4, 0)$.
Now $\text{DN} = 6\text{ units}$
and
$$\text{NO} = \sqrt{(-10 - 0)^2 + (4 - 0)^2 + (0 - 0)^2} = \sqrt{(-10)^2 + 4^2 + 0^2} = \sqrt{116}\text{ units}$$
$$\therefore \tan\theta = \frac{6}{\sqrt{116}}$$
$$\therefore \theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{6}{\sqrt{116}}\right) \approx 29.1^{\circ}$$
The angle is about $29.1^{\circ}$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: To find the angle a line makes with a coordinate plane, project the line onto that plane and calculate the angle in the resulting right triangle.
step_by_step: The orthogonal projection of D$(-10, 4, 6)$ on the xy-plane is $\text{N}(-10, 4, 0)$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Using the distance OD directly in the tangent function instead of the adjacent side ON.

subparts.stem: Find the angle between the following line segments and the base plane BECO: [EM]

mark_breakdown.desc: Identify coordinates of P and calculate distances MP and PE
Set up tan ratio for angle MEP

subparts.solution:
The required angle is $\text{M}\hat{\text{E}}\text{P}$, where $\text{P}$ has coordinates $(-5, 4, 0)$.
Now $\text{MP} = 6\text{ units}$
and
$$\text{PE} = \sqrt{(-10 - (-5))^2 + (8 - 4)^2 + (0 - 0)^2} = \sqrt{(-5)^2 + 4^2 + 0^2} = \sqrt{41}\text{ units}$$
$$\therefore \tan\theta = \frac{6}{\sqrt{41}}$$
$$\therefore \theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{6}{\sqrt{41}}\right) \approx 43.1^{\circ}$$
The angle is about $43.1^{\circ}$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The angle between a line segment and the base plane is the angle between the segment and its projection on the base plane.
step_by_step: The projection of M$(-5, 4, 6)$ onto the base plane is $\text{P}(-5, 4, 0)$.
The projection length $\text{PE}$ is found using distance formula between $\text{P}(-5, 4, 0)$ and $\text{E}(-10, 8, 0)$: $\text{PE} = \sqrt{(-5)^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{41}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Incorrect coordinates for projection point P or the vertex E.
